title: Governance Track: Pricing, SLA & Integration Planning
summary: Kickoff for vendor onboarding covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations (uptime & latency), pricing approval path, and technical integration constraints (VPC, KMS, egress). Agreed to run a 30-day pilot on Dedicated with capped egress; Redwood to circulate MSA redlines and security packet.
topics: Pricing approval workflow and committed usage
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Sam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lin (Horizon Legal), Dana Holt (Horizon Procurement), Luis Ortega (Horizon PM)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Sam - Redwood AE): Okay, thanks everyone for joining, we can see a full house, so I'll kick us off. Today's agenda is to align on the governance path for getting Redwood onboarded – MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing approval steps, and the technical constraints for the pilot.

00:28 Speaker 2 (Marcus - Horizon Legal): Yep, thanks Sam. Quick note, sorry if audio is a bit rough, connection flaked earlier. We're mostly focused on the DPA questions around data residency and retention, and the MSA section on indemnity and liability caps.

00:45 Speaker 3 (Priya - Redwood SE): Hi all, Priya here. I'll be the technical lead from Redwood on the integration. I want to surface a few items: if you're planning a VPC/private plane deployment we'll need to talk about KMS integration and the HSM workflow. Also egress assumptions — they matter for pricing.

01:10 Speaker 4 (Dana - Procurement): Hi, Dana from procurement. Process-wise we need a pricing sheet and the MSA with redlines to go to our procurement council by Tuesday. Pricing must show committed monthly spend and a breakout of the egress and storage components.

01:35 Speaker 1 (Sam): Understood. We can provide a redline MSA and a pricing deck. For the pilot we usually propose a 30-day Dedicated pilot with a capped egress allowance to keep procurement comfortable.

01:58 Speaker 5 (Luis - Horizon PM): Curious on SLA specifics — our uptime bar for production is 99.95% and P99 latency under 350ms for interactive use. Is that realistic for Dedicated?

02:15 Speaker 3 (Priya): 99.95% is achievable on Dedicated pools with the right autoscaling config and throughput reservation. Latency depends on model choice; for smaller seq lengths for chat it's doable. We can run benchmarks against your tail latencies during the pilot.

02:48 Speaker 2 (Marcus): On the MSA indemnity language — we need to cap at the contract value, standard for us. Also, we have a clause request about data access by subcontractors — need to see how Redwood handles vendor subprocessors.

03:12 Speaker 1 (Sam): We have a subprocessors list and SOC2 reports. We'll share the security packet and SOC2 Type II report. For indemnity, we can propose a mutual cap aligned to the first 12 months of committed spend, which helps both sides.

03:35 Speaker 4 (Dana): That could work but procurement will push for higher, we'll need to see the numbers. Also, any SSO options? We need SAML or OIDC with SCIM provisioning ideally.

03:50 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for user management. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS via KeyWrap or customer HSM – we'll document the KMS flows in the security packet.

04:15 Speaker 5 (Luis): About data residency — some of our data is EU-only. Can a private deployment be provisioned in eu-west-1 and ensure logs don't leave region?

04:32 Speaker 1 (Sam): Yes, we can pin the private control plane region and configure logging to an EU region. We'll need the DPA to specify data flows; we'll propose EU-processing addendum language.

04:58 Speaker 2 (Marcus): On e-discovery and audit logs, legal will want 90 days of immutable audit logs accessible for export. Is that standard?

05:15 Speaker 3 (Priya): Audit retention is configurable; 90 days is within default options but for longer retention we usually have an add-on. We can enable export to your S3 bucket in the region for custody.

05:38 Speaker 4 (Dana): Pricing — can you give a ballpark for Dedicated baseline? We need a number to present.

05:48 Speaker 1 (Sam): Ballpark for a small Dedicated pool with moderate concurrency is $25k/month committed for X GPUs effective, with egress billed separately; for the pilot we can do a reduced pilot rate with egress cap to limit initial spend. We'll send a detailed sheet.

06:12 Speaker 5 (Luis): Is there a model on reserved vs burst capacity for handling spikes? We get unpredictable spikes during end-of-quarter reporting.

06:28 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes, Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling policies. You can reserve baseline capacity and allow controlled burst into hosted capacity or other pools with routing rules. We'll draft recommended autoscale policy for your workload pattern.

06:58 Speaker 2 (Marcus): Quick procedural Q from legal — what's your standard SLA credit process and how do we prove downtime? We need an objective metric in the contract.

07:12 Speaker 1 (Sam): SLA credits are issued based on measured downtime against the per-month window. We'll include the telemetry hooks and agreed measurement signals. We also support a third-party uptime verification feed if that's required.

07:40 Speaker 4 (Dana): Our procurement committee wants to know about tax and billing entity — can Redwood invoice us in USD to the US legal entity or do you require EU invoicing?

07:56 Speaker 1 (Sam): We can invoice the US entity; for EU residency we can route data regionally but billing can be centralized. We'll clarify with Finance and include options in the pricing sheet.

08:20 Speaker 5 (Luis): Integration items — what network setup is required for Private deployment? VPC peering, specific ports?

08:32 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll provide a network runbook. Typically it's a managed VPC with customer peering, or a direct connect setup for on-prem. Ports are standard TLS endpoints; we'll share a checklist.

08:58 Speaker 2 (Marcus): DPA wording — we need deletion timelines, subprocessors list, and clarity on aggregated telemetry. Also, can we get an option to certify deletion on deprovision?

09:18 Speaker 1 (Sam): We can provide the subprocessors list and deletion procedures. For deprovisioning, we can provide attestation for data erasure per DPA, with logs. We'll put language in the DPA addendum.

09:42 Speaker 4 (Dana): Timeline — if we push this to procurement next Tuesday, how fast can the legal redline turnaround be?

09:55 Speaker 1 (Sam): We aim for 72 hours after you send redlines for the initial counters, faster if it's just comments. We'll try to accelerate since you have a procurement council next week.

10:20 Speaker 5 (Luis): Pilot acceptance criteria — what constitutes success for the 30-day pilot?

10:30 Speaker 3 (Priya): Proposed success criteria: 1) meets latency SLOs P99 under agreed threshold, 2) stable throughput for your expected concurrent users, 3) successful KMS integration and no data egress violations, 4) security review signoff.

10:55 Speaker 2 (Marcus): For indemnity we need to loop in our risk team; I noted mutual cap tied to committed spend but may need to be higher.

11:08 Speaker 1 (Sam): We'll propose mutual cap at 12x committed monthly spend as a starting point; open to discussion.

11:25 Speaker 4 (Dana): About SLA credits, our finance needs to see how credits translate into refunds vs service credits.

11:38 Speaker 1 (Sam): We typically issue service credits applied to invoice, but can discuss cash refunds at enterprise tier. We'll note that in the MSA options.

11:58 Speaker 5 (Luis): Security review — do you have an up-to-date penetration test report?

12:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): We have a recent pentest summary and full reports under NDA. We'll include summary in the security packet and can provide full docs on an NDA.

12:30 Speaker 2 (Marcus): Any special clauses around export controls? We have customers in restricted geos and need to ensure compliance.

12:45 Speaker 1 (Sam): Export controls are managed; we'll include standard representation and will add language for geofencing and restricted dataflows as required.

13:05 Speaker 4 (Dana): Procurement asks — can you confirm the termination notice period and what happens to data on termination?

13:22 Speaker 1 (Sam): Standard 60 days notice for annual contracts, 30 for shorter pilots; data is retained per DPA and can be exported prior to deletion. We'll include a data export runbook in the onboarding pack.

13:48 Speaker 5 (Luis): Are there any pre-approved SOC2 or ISO stamps we can reference?

14:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 are in our compliance portfolio. We'll share certs via the secure portal link.

14:20 Speaker 2 (Marcus): Regarding subprocessors — do you allow cherry-picking to exclude any subprocessor? Our legal policy sometimes requires that for specific data types.

14:38 Speaker 1 (Sam): We can discuss, but completely excluding a core subprocessor could impact service. For non-core ones we can explore alternatives. We'll call out which are critical.

15:00 Speaker 4 (Dana): Next, pricing approvals — do you offer a procurement worksheet showing committed vs on-demand cost across scenarios? We want something quantitative.

15:14 Speaker 1 (Sam): Yes we'll provide a price modeling spreadsheet with scenarios: 1) committed baseline, 2) burst behavior estimated, 3) egress and storage breakout. We'll tailor it to your estimated QPS and payload sizes.

15:36 Speaker 5 (Luis): For the pilot, what's the minimum telemetry hooks you need us to enable to run the latency benchmarks?

15:46 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll need sample traffic, representative prompts, and access to latency traces (we can SSH into a metrics stream or push dashboards). We'll send a minimal instrumentation checklist.

16:08 Speaker 2 (Marcus): Any data residency SLA specifics we should request in the DPA? We want a commitment that EU-data doesn't leave region except for backups with consent.

16:22 Speaker 1 (Sam): We'll propose language for data-in-region with explicit backup exceptions requiring written consent.

16:40 Speaker 4 (Dana): Are there any discounts for multi-year committed contracts? Procurement asks for tiered discounts.

16:52 Speaker 1 (Sam): Yes multi-year discounts are standard; we'll show a 10-15% for 12-month commits and higher for multi-year. Exact numbers in the pricing sheet.

17:12 Speaker 5 (Luis): What about RTO/RPO for your backups? We need specifics for our SRE runbook.

17:26 Speaker 3 (Priya): RTO/RPO vary by deployment but target RPO under 24 hours and RTO under 4 hours for Dedicated critical data. We'll add specifics to the runbook.

17:50 Speaker 2 (Marcus): Legal will want to markup the DPA and MSA; can we get editable Word docs?

17:58 Speaker 1 (Sam): Yes we'll share Word redlines for both MSA and DPA. Expect them in the next 24 hours to help hit your procurement deadline.

18:20 Speaker 4 (Dana): Any concerns about egress charges during the pilot? We need a hard cap so budget doesn't blow up.

18:33 Speaker 1 (Sam): We can put a provisional egress cap for the pilot and monitor; if you hit it we'll pause or renegotiate. We'll add that to the pilot addendum.

18:58 Speaker 5 (Luis): Who will be the day-to-day contact for technical questions during the pilot?

19:08 Speaker 3 (Priya): That'll be me, Priya. I'll be on call for runbook handoffs and daily check-ins during the first two weeks.

19:25 Speaker 2 (Marcus): Any quick wins we can do now to make legal comfortable — e.g., predetermined SLA metrics or indemnity language templates?

19:38 Speaker 1 (Sam): We'll include suggested SLA language and mutual indemnity cap options in the draft MSA so your counsel has something concrete to react to.

19:58 Speaker 4 (Dana): Ok, timeline recap please?

20:05 Speaker 1 (Sam): Sure: Redwood to send MSA/DPA Word redlines, pricing sheet, security packet (SOC2, pentest summary), and pilot addendum by end-of-day Friday 2025-10-03. Horizon to review and provide initial redlines to legal and procurement by 2025-10-07. Pilot target start: 2025-10-15 pending approvals.

20:30 Speaker 5 (Luis): That timeline helps. We'll try to prioritize the procurement council slot.

20:42 Speaker 3 (Priya): Technical note: I'll attach the VPC runbook and minimal instrumentation checklist to the packet.

20:55 Speaker 2 (Marcus): Legal follow-up — please add the subprocessors list and the DPA EU addendum draft.

21:08 Speaker 1 (Sam): Noted. Anything else?

21:20 Speaker 4 (Dana): One more — support SLAs: do you have 24x7 enterprise support for critical incidents? Procurement will ask for escalation matrix.

21:32 Speaker 3 (Priya): Enterprise customers get 24x7 on-call with escalation path to SREs and a named CSM for priority routing. We'll include the escalation matrix.

21:55 Speaker 5 (Luis): Good. Let's capture action items and close out.

22:05 Speaker 1 (Sam): I'll do a quick recap and next steps.

22:10 Speaker 1 (Sam): Recap: Redwood to deliver MSA and DPA redlines (Word), pricing workbook with committed and burst scenarios, security packet (SOC2 + pentest), VPC/runbook and instrumentation checklist, pilot addendum with egress cap, subprocessors list, and sample SLA language by 2025-10-03. Horizon will review and return redlines by 2025-10-07. Target pilot start 2025-10-15.

22:48 Speaker 2 (Marcus): Thanks, that's clear. We'll loop in our risk team offline.

23:02 Speaker 4 (Dana): Thanks everyone. Dana out.

23:07 Speaker 3 (Priya): Thanks all, Priya signing off after I drop the runbook.

23:12 Speaker 1 (Sam): Thanks team, Sam out.

23:20 End of recording.
